story: At 6:17 on this humid, hazy Thursday in Sumter Oaks, Gary is bench-testing light strip wiring and a speaker module at his workbench, leaving his golf cart untouched until he gets approval. Donna is out on pickleball court one, drilling serve returns and deep dinks so she'll be ready to coach Gary when he shows up. Hal is walking Magnolia Loop, dutifully counting each pink flamingo in the Donna flock he can see from the street. Meanwhile, Rosa is at the town square parade signup table, hopefully putting her cart's name down for Saturday's 6 PM parade.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Bench-build and test the cart's light strip wiring and speaker module, parked cart untouched until approval
Donna (pickleball court 1): Practice serve returns and deep dinks so I can coach Gary when he shows up
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count each flamingo visible from the street and record the total
Rosa (parade signup table): Sign our parade cart up for Saturday's 6 PM parade

gary.thought_process: I'm back home at the workbench with nobody around, and the Architectural Review decision still isn't posted. L-01 means the cart stays unmodified on the street side until approval, so I can't put lights or speakers on the exterior yet. But I can do bench work: build the sound system module and test the wiring on the workbench, which is out of sight and breaks no rule. It's 6:17 PM, well before quiet hours, and I'll keep volume low anyway. Rosa's Thursday table is coming up and Saturday is close, so I should use this hour productively and be ready to install the moment approval lands.

parameters.content: Bench-build and test the cart's light strip wiring and speaker module, parked cart untouched until approval

donna.thought_process: I've already reserved the court, warmed up with dinking drills, and practiced third-shot drops. Gary isn't here yet and nobody's in sight. No sense asking again or calling out to an empty court. I should keep my time useful and not repeat myself. The ladder standings board is right here, and I've glanced at it once, but a quick look at the Pruitt-Kowalski gap could sharpen our game plan for the match. Actually, a better use of the hour is to keep drilling the serve-return so I can coach Gary properly when he arrives, since he's never played.

parameters.content: Practice serve returns and deep dinks so I can coach Gary when he shows up

hal.thought_process: I've been standing here counting flamingos for two ticks now without writing down a total, and a watchdog with no number has no case. The committee sits tomorrow. Gary's cart application is with Rosa and he's promised nothing goes on the street side until they sign off, so I'll take him at his word until I see otherwise. Donna's flock is another matter. L-02 says three ornaments visible from the street, and I intend to have an exact count in hand, straight and fair, before I say a word to anyone. Time to look at the flock and get it done.

parameters.content: Count each flamingo visible from the street and record the total

rosa.thought_process: I just handed in the parade cart folder at Town Hall with Gary's clamp list, light layout, and a plain description of the tuck-on decorations, so the review part is done and I walked back to the Square. Nobody is around. The parade signup table is right here, and with Halloween on the Loop on Saturday the cart should be on the list. Signing up is the next concrete step toward the parade and toward keeping Donna, Gary and Hal together on this project, rather than standing around waiting.

parameters.content: Sign our parade cart up for Saturday's 6 PM parade

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
